title: Batch orchestrator ledger
description: Batch history for one programme's build run. Lives at <workarea>/orchestrator-ledger.json. Written only by L0. Records what each batch actually built; backlog.json remains the plan of record for increment truth. A batch is a budget, not a plan — L0 hands L1 a count and L1 re-derives the next increment after every landing, so the ids are known only as they land.

programme.description: The parameters a fresh L0 needs to resume without asking anyone.

workarea.description: Path under workareas/ holding backlog.json, e.g. shared/plant-products-ched-pp

branch.description: The branch every repo in the programme is cut onto

batchSize.description: The default per-batch budget — the MOST increments an L1 may build before returning. Not a target. Default 5

batches.description: Append-only, oldest first. Batch numbers are contiguous from 1.

budget.description: The count L0 handed L1 — the most increments it was allowed to build. Known before the batch starts, unlike the ids

startCounts.description: Backlog counts as L0 measured them when opening the batch. Lets a later reader compute a batch's progress without re-querying, and survives a dead L1

attempted.description: The ids L1 actually started, in the order it derived them. Absent while in flight. Kept alongside landed/notLanded because those two do not cover an increment L1 died partway through — reconciling an abandoned batch needs the list of ids to check against git. An id may legitimately appear here in more than one batch: a failed increment is retried by a later batch

status.description: in-flight = L1 spawned, not yet reported. landed = every increment L1 attempted landed. partial = some landed, then it stopped. failed = none landed. halted-at-gate = the loop stopped at a designed gate. abandoned = L1 died and L0 reconciled from git plus backlog.json. A batch that lands fewer increments than its budget is NOT partial — partial is about failure, not about spending the budget

endedEarly.description: Why L1 stopped. budget-spent means it used its full allowance; every other value means it returned early on purpose, which is a normal and desirable outcome

driver.description: How L1 drove L2 — the increment-build-loop Workflow, or the documented Codex fallback

scriptPath.description: The script the Workflow ran, normally the batch's fresh run copy at workareas/<workarea>/build-loop.run.js. Recorded alongside driver so a batch can be traced to the script that produced it. Absent when driver is codex-direct

commit.description: Short SHA, verified by L0 against git log — not copied from L1's report unchecked

repo.description: The increment's repo field: frontend, backend or tests

stash.description: The stash ref the rollback produced, so the work is recoverable

report.description: Workarea-relative path to L1's full batch report, e.g. logs/batches/batch-003.md. L0 records the path and does not read the file
